audit.whatIsWrong: The entry gives Ryze a spell shield he does not have. spikes[3] says he "spellshields your Repudiation slam"; mid says "Hold the ult until his spellshield is down, or he simply eats the blink-suppress on a shielded instance"; late says he "spellshields your Repudiation slam to deny the amp"; wants.you[1] says to burst him "before his spellshield comes back up"; wants.foe[1] instructs him to "Hold the spellshield for her Repudiation slam or her R"; whys[4] and whys[6] repeat it.
audit.why: Ryze has no spell shield in any slot. His abilities are Arcane Mastery, Overload, Rune Prison, Spell Flux and Realm Warp, and none of them block a spell — champ-data/_kits/ryze.json carries no spellShield flag anywhere. The only spell shield in the matchup is Banshee's Veil, an item he may or may not build. The consequence is severe: mid tells the reader to hold a 130-second ultimate waiting for a cooldown that does not exist, which means never using it.
audit.corrected: Every reference to a Ryze spell shield removed and replaced with Banshee's Veil named as an item, where relevant. The instruction to hold R for it is gone.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ryze.json (full ability list, no spellShield flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: The root is called the "Q-E root" or "Q-into-E root" in nine places across both layers. Neither Q nor E is the root.
audit.why: Riot's Rune Prison (W) text: "Ryze traps a target in a cage of runes, damaging them and slowing their movement. If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted." So the root is W, and it only roots when Spell Flux (E) is already applied — otherwise it is just a slow. Overload (Q) is a 1000-range line projectile and has nothing to do with it. This is the single most actionable fact in the matchup and it is inverted: the tell to dash on is the Spell Flux orb, one cast BEFORE the cage, and a reader watching for the wrong ability dashes a beat too late every time.
audit.corrected: Named correctly throughout, with the Flux-then-Prison dependency stated as the dash cue, and the real cooldowns attached — Rune Prison 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, Spell Flux 3.5 down to 2.5.

audit.whatIsWrong: Realm Warp is described as an escape that Public Execution "hard-cancels" — in spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1], whys[4] and late ("uses realm-warp to disengage or flank").
audit.why: Riot's Realm Warp text: "Ryze creates a portal to a nearby location. After a few seconds, allies standing near the portal are teleported to the target location." It is a delayed group teleport on a 180/160/140 cooldown, not a blink and not a channel — there is no escape to intercept mid-flight. What actually beats it is keeping him away from his own portal until it fires, which a suppress does. Telling the reader their ultimate cancels it invites them to spend a 130-second cooldown on a cancel that will not happen.
audit.corrected: Restated as a delayed portal with the 180s cooldown, and the level-6 advice repointed at holding him off the portal rather than cancelling anything.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ryze.json (R, cd 180/160/140, range 3000, no channel flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1] again credit Public Execution with "R's bonus armor pen" and "the heal-on-ability passive topping you off" / "the passive heals you on every hit".
audit.why: Public Execution blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, suppresses on arrival, then slams for damage and a stun. No penetration, no healing. Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund. Against a mage this matters twice over — the reader is promised sustain through poke that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the crash stun, which is the real reason the follow-up lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0].why says "Empowered-hit weaving wins the early AA exchanges" under a stage the chart itself gives to Ryze, and phases[1].why repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield" error. No cooldown number appears anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Ryze outranges Ambessa 1000 to 650 with Overload and there is no auto-attack exchange to win at level 1. And the spike story is a cooldown story the entry never tells: Spell Flux is 3.5s falling to 2.5s so the root setup is always available, Overload is 5s and is reset by his other casts so the poke never stops, and Rune Prison is the only ability with a real gap at 11s down to 9s.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten; real numbers added to spikes, whys, breakdown.cooldowns and the do/don't descriptions.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagrees with its own whys[] at three stages. It gives Ambessa levels 4-5 while whys[3] says "Levels 4-5 are his"; it gives Ryze level 6 while whys[4] calls it Ambessa's clean burst window; and it gives Ambessa the two-item stage while whys[6] says "2+ items belong to him".
audit.why: At 50.25% over 402 games the lane is even overall but strongly staged — Ryze scales and Ambessa's window is 6 through first item. The packet levelChart (Skill, Skill, Ambessa, Ryze, Ambessa, Ambessa, Ryze) matches the prose. As written the chart tells the reader to fight the two windows the text tells them to concede, and to concede the one window the text says is theirs.
audit.corrected: Not changed. "Ambessa" is 7 characters and "Ryze" is 4, so all three flips cross the length band in both directions and the applier would reject them. Documented in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1], dosFull[2] and all three dontsFull descriptions are stock boilerplate unrelated to their titles — "Trade without passive loaded" is explained as "Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown", and "R into peel" as the generic "duelist who forgot the door" line.
audit.why: All five have concrete answers in the kits: Rune Prison reaches 615 units, Drakehound's Step needs a cast to fire at all, and Realm Warp has no mid-flight moment to catch.
audit.corrected: All five rewritten with real ranges, the Flux tell, and the passive's actual trigger.

edits.before: Ryze out-ranges you at levels 1-2, so farm with the tip of your Cunning Sweep cone and eat as little Q poke as possible instead of stepping into his root range. At level 3 you finally have a kit: bait his Q-E root, dash out of the snare with a move command mid-cast (Drakehound's Step), then close with Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam and a Lacerate spin so its near-total slow keeps him pinned for an empowered auto. Never walk up while his root is available — getting snared at range is exactly how he pokes you out without taking damage back.
edits.after: Ryze out-ranges you at levels 1-2 — Overload throws 1000 units and your Cunning Sweep reaches 650 — so farm with the tip of the cone instead of stepping into Rune Prison range. At level 3 you finally have a kit: the root only lands if Spell Flux is on you first, so the orb is your warning, not the cage. Bait it, dash out with a move command mid-cast (Drakehound's Step), then close with Cunning Sweep into Sundering Slam and a Lacerate spin so its near-total slow keeps him pinned for an empowered auto.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 lean Ryze: your cooldowns are at their longest and his Q-E root cycles back before your trade resets, so concede a little CS and farm toward 6 rather than forcing a losing poke war. At 6 it swings your way — Public Execution blinks you behind him and suppresses him, hard-cancelling his realm-warp and letting you crash him down with R's bonus armor pen while the passive heals you on every hit. Hold the ult until his spellshield is down, or he simply eats the blink-suppress on a shielded instance and you waste your whole burst window.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 lean Ryze: your cooldowns are at their longest and Rune Prison is back every 10s while Overload resets off every other cast, so concede a little CS and farm toward 6. At 6 it swings your way — Public Execution blinks to him and suppresses him, and the crash stun holds him for the whole follow-up. Realm Warp is a 180s portal that fires a few seconds after the cast, not an instant escape, so a suppress that keeps him away from it is the answer. He has no spell shield of his own — only Banshee's Veil if he buys it.

notes:
The packet defect line ("never names any of Ryze's abilities") understates the problem. The names were missing, but the mechanics attached to the unnamed abilities were also wrong in three separate ways: a spell shield Ryze does not possess (7 strings), a root credited to Q and E when it is W and requires E first (9 strings), and an ultimate described as an escape when it is a delayed group teleport (5 strings). Naming the abilities alone would not have fixed any of it.

COULD NOT FIT IN THE BAND, for the user to apply by hand: content win[3], win[4], win[6] and full phases[3].side, phases[4].side, phases[6].side. They should read Ryze, Ambessa, Ryze respectively, matching both the packet levelChart and this entry's own whys[3], whys[4] and whys[6]. "Ambessa" is 7 characters and "Ryze" is 4, so every swap crosses +/-10%.

focus.letters is ["W"] and focus.text is "Ryze Rune Prison" — those are correct as far as they go, but the ability the reader actually needs to watch is Spell Flux (E), since Rune Prison without it is only a slow. I left focus alone rather than point it at an ability that does not itself do the rooting.
